name: Fixed polite expressions
definition: Learn greetings, courteous responses, naming expressions and classroom requests as complete chunks. Choose the chunk matching the situation. A fixed chunk does not license changing its adjective, case or verb form; productive inflection is introduced later.

name: Present-tense identity without a copula
definition: In a simple present-tense identity statement, a subject pronoun can be followed directly by a nominative name or noun, normally without a word corresponding to English am, is or are. This lesson practices naming a person; possession, location, past and future reference require additional patterns.

name: Identification with это
definition: Use это followed by a nominative naming expression to identify a person, object or printed numeral. In this pattern, это stays unchanged even before a feminine noun. This is not the rule for a demonstrative modifier agreeing with a following noun.

name: Subject pronouns and reference
definition: Use я, ты, он, она, оно, мы, вы and они as subject forms. Ты addresses one familiar person; вы addresses several people or one person politely. Он, она and оно can also refer to things according to grammatical gender. Subject pronouns precede the naming expression in the initial identity models. Do not insert an English-style present-tense copula.

name: Basic noun gender
definition: Learn the gender with each noun. A final consonant or -й usually marks masculine nouns; -а or -я usually marks feminine nouns; -о or -е usually marks neuter nouns. A final soft sign does not determine gender on its own. Папа is masculine despite -а, and имя is neuter despite -я. These are patterns for taught nouns, not an exception-free guessing rule.

name: Basic written questions
definition: A yes-no question can retain statement word order and end with a question mark. Question words identify missing information: кто asks about a person, что about a thing, где about location, как about manner or a name pattern, and откуда about origin. Later question words follow the same information-seeking principle. Do not add an English-style auxiliary. Choose the question word for the requested information, not merely for the expected answer's first word.

name: Basic genitive forms
definition: Use the genitive after из for origin, after a naming noun for possession or association, and after нет for absence. Common singular patterns are consonant masculine + -а, masculine -й or -ь to -я, feminine -а to -ы or -и, feminine -я or -ь to -и, neuter -о to -а, and neuter -е to -я. Nouns in -ия take -ии. Apply the spelling rule that uses и rather than ы after г, к, х, ж, ч, ш and щ. Learn pronoun forms such as меня, тебя, нас and вас separately. Plural forms and exceptions must be supplied rather than guessed.

name: Dative recipients and age
definition: The dative identifies a recipient in taught verb patterns and the person whose age is stated. Use мне for я, тебе for ты, ему for он, ей for она, нам for мы and вам for вы. A simple age statement has the person in the dative followed by the number and the appropriate year form. Common noun patterns include masculine or neuter -у or -ю, feminine -а or -я to -е, feminine -ь to -и, and -ия to -ии. Practice recipient constructions only with verbs whose corresponding use has been taught.

name: Numbers and basic time notation
definition: In nominative or inanimate-accusative counting phrases, 1 selects singular, 2-4 select genitive singular, and 5-20 select genitive plural. Larger numbers follow their final component, but endings 11-14 still select genitive plural. Learn год, года and лет as the year forms. Learn один, одна, одно and два, две as the supplied gender forms in nominative counting; oblique numeral declension is not taught here. Apply the same supplied-form method to hours and minutes. Read clock notation as HH:MM and the explicitly labeled date format as DD.MM.YYYY. Weekday expressions use the accusative with the preposition for on; month expressions use the prepositional with in; taught season time forms use the instrumental. Do not require an untaught calendar word or a spoken ordinal date.

name: Possession with у + genitive
definition: Possession uses у followed by the possessor in the genitive: У меня есть книга. In the present tense есть may be omitted: У меня книга. With нет the possessed item takes the genitive: У меня нет книги. Use only the supplied genitive forms of taught nouns; do not guess endings.

name: Possessive pronouns мой, твой, наш
definition: мой, твой and наш agree with the thing possessed in gender and number: мой брат, моя сестра, наше дело. его and её do not change: его сестра, её брат. Learn each supplied agreement form as a chunk; do not decline его or её.

name: Location with в/на + prepositional
definition: Where is asked with где and answered with в or на followed by the prepositional case: Где комната? — В комнате. На кухне есть чайник. Learn the prepositional form of each taught noun as supplied (комната → комнате, кухня → кухне, стол → столе); do not guess endings.

name: Choosing в versus на
definition: в names being inside something (в комнате, в шкафу); на names being on a surface or in an open area (на столе, на кухне, на улице). Some taught places take на by convention (на кухне, на улице); learn the pairing together with the noun rather than translating from English.

name: Telling the time
definition: The time is asked with Сколько времени? and answered with Сейчас plus a number: Сейчас три часа. The noun changes with the number in the supplied forms (один час, два часа, пять часов); learn each supplied pairing and do not build new ones. Day parts appear as utrom and vecherom in the taught forms.

name: Frequency adverbs before the verb
definition: всегда, часто, иногда, редко and никогда normally stand before the verb: Я всегда читаю. Она часто гуляет. Learn the word order as a chunk; the adverb itself never changes form.
